title: Minimum Deletions to Make Character Frequencies Unique
summary: Determine the least number of deletions required to ensure no two distinct characters in a string have the same frequency.
statement: Determine the least number of deletions required to ensure no two distinct characters in a string have the same frequency. The frequency of a character is its count in the string.
constraints: Delete the fewest characters so all remaining positive character frequencies are distinct; characters may be deleted entirely.
hints: For each frequency, the best available replacement is the largest unused value no greater than it.
Process counts high to low and decrement collisions until reaching an unused positive count or zero.
Record positive kept counts and accumulate every decrement.
Choosing a smaller available count would only add deletions and cannot create more room for later, no-larger frequencies.
editorial: Choosing a smaller available count would only add deletions and cannot create more room for later, no-larger frequencies.

tests.explanation: Frequencies two and one are already distinct, so no deletion is needed.
Reduce one frequency three to two and the original frequency two to one, using two deletions.
